transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Yeah, uh… I came in because I just feel like I got a motor running inside me all day. Like I can’t just be still. If I’m sitting at church, or waiting here at the clinic, or even just at home, it starts feeling like I’m trapped in my own body or something, and I gotta get up, move around, do something.

It’s hard to explain… like, other folks can just sit there, and I’m watching the clock or shifting around, thinking about needing to stand up. Even at church, you know, I try to be respectful, but my legs are going, and then I’m thinking about the pews and how they creak—sorry, that’s not the point. The point is I just can’t sit still, and it’s been wearing me out.
Have you started or changed the dose of any medications recently, especially antipsychotics or anti-nausea drugs, around the time this restlessness began?

Um… I don’t think so? I mean, I’m not real good with the names of medicines, to be honest. If it’s one of those long names on the bottle, I usually just—well, my aunt used to keep all her bottles lined up by the sink and I always thought that was a bad spot because they get wet, you know?

But no, I don’t remember starting anything new or changing a dose around when this got bad. At least not that I noticed. What kind of anti-nausea medicine do you mean?
Does this restless feeling tend to get worse in the evening or at night, and do you notice it's specifically your legs that feel like they need to move, with relief when you do move them?

I don’t know that it’s just evenings or nights, really. It feels like it’s all day, like I’ve got this motor in me. If I’m stuck sitting—church, here at the clinic, even at home—I start feeling kind of trapped and I need to get up or do something.

My legs do move a lot, I guess, but it’s not only like my legs at night or anything. It’s more like my whole self can’t settle. Like, even those church pews, once you’re in there and everybody’s quiet, I start thinking I gotta stand up, but then I’m worried folks will look over—anyway, yeah, it’s just hard to sit still.
Besides this need to move, do you also find yourself worrying a lot, most days, about different things—like health, family, or work—even when there's no clear reason to?

I mean… I don’t know. I worry some, like anybody does, I guess, but I can’t say it’s most days about health or work or all that. Work’s kind of a whole other thing, but—well, my cousin used to say if you don’t worry, you’re not paying attention, which I never really understood because he worried about everything, even the weather.

But no, I’m not sure it’s like that for me. I haven’t really noticed a bunch of worrying for no reason. It’s more just… hard to settle, I guess.
Did you feel this same kind of restlessness back when you were a kid or teenager, or is this something that started more recently, like in the past few weeks or months?

Oh, no, this ain’t brand new. I was like that as a kid too. In school, the teachers were always moving my seat around because I couldn’t stay put. I’d be talking when I wasn’t supposed to, or I’d jump up before class was even over.

I remember one teacher put me right up front by her desk, like that was gonna fix it, but then I’d just mess with stuff on her desk or turn around anyway. So yeah… it goes way back, not just the last few weeks.
Aside from the restlessness, do you still have trouble focusing, finishing tasks, or acting impulsively now as an adult, the way you did back in school?

Yeah, I do. Like, I’ll say I’m gonna run an errand for my aunt or help out with something at the pantry, and I’ll get going on it, but then I only do the first part. Then somehow the rest just… falls out of my head.

And later somebody’s asking, “Did you finish that?” and I’m standing there realizing I didn’t. It’s embarrassing. I don’t mean to leave folks hanging. I’ll have every intention of doing it, but then I get pulled into something else or I forget there was more to it.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports lifelong (since childhood) pervasive restlessness, inability to sit still, inattention (starting tasks but not finishing, forgetting steps), and impulsivity (blurting out, jumping up in class) that persist into adulthood across multiple settings (school, church, clinic, home). Symptoms are not confined to evening/night, not relieved specifically by leg movement (ruling out RLS), not temporally linked to a new medication (ruling out akathisia), and not accompanied by pervasive uncontrollable worry (ruling out GAD). The chronic, cross-situational, developmental pattern with early childhood onset and functional impairment (embarrassment, unfinished tasks) supports a hyperkinetic disorder diagnosis.
